blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, accounting stops being a reporting function and becomes the language in which the whole company decides. A board that speaks it well can debate strategy in specific, testable terms — margin, capital employed, cash conversion, return on invested capital. A board that does not speaks in adjectives — 'strong', 'healthy', 'promising' — and makes decisions nobody can quite evaluate later.

The senior finance leader's job is to teach the board this language, patiently and without condescension. Not all directors arrive fluent. Many are excellent operators who have simply never been given the definitions clearly. A month of quiet explanation, one ratio at a time, transforms the quality of every board conversation for years.

Accounting at the top is not about knowing more. It is about giving everyone in the room the same words, the same definitions, and the same ability to test any claim against the numbers.

items.q: According to the text, what does accounting become at executive level?
options: A reporting function that summarises the past
The language in which the whole company decides
A compliance obligation imposed by regulators
A specialism reserved for the finance department
items.why: "accounting stops being a reporting function and becomes the language in which the whole company decides."

items.q: How does a board that does NOT speak the language make its decisions?
options: By deferring entirely to the auditors
By avoiding financial questions altogether
In adjectives such as 'strong' or 'promising'
In specific, testable terms
items.why: "speaks in adjectives — 'strong', 'healthy', 'promising' — and makes decisions nobody can quite evaluate later."

items.q: The author suggests that directors who are not fluent in accounting are most likely…
options: deliberately kept in the dark by the finance team
uninterested in the company's strategy
capable operators who were never given the definitions clearly
incompetent and unfit for the board
items.why: Inferência: "Many are excellent operators who have simply never been given the definitions clearly." — a falta é de ensino, não de capacidade.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Fluency in accounting can be taught one ratio at a time.
Shared definitions improve the quality of board debate.
Teaching a director the numbers is beneath a senior finance leader.
Adjectives make financial claims hard to evaluate.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste em ensinar "without condescension" — para o autor, ensinar a diretoria é parte do trabalho, não algo indigno.

items.q: What does the closing line — "the same ability to test any claim against the numbers" — imply about the purpose of this shared language?
options: It exists to make finance look more authoritative than operations
It ensures only the CFO can challenge a proposal
It lets any assertion be checked, rather than merely asserted
It replaces judgement with arithmetic
items.why: Inferência: "testable" e "test any claim" — a linguagem comum serve para que qualquer afirmação possa ser verificada contra os números.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James apresentando um glossário de uma página a uma nova conselheira. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for the twenty minutes — I know the diligence pack landed on you last night. I've put everything you'll actually need onto a single page, so let me walk you through it rather than leave you to decode the jargon alone.

Start at the top. Margin is simply profit as a share of revenue — nothing clever, but be careful which margin someone means, because gross and operating are very different animals. Beneath that I've written capital employed: think of it as the money the business is actually using to run — not what it raised, but what is tied up right now.

The two I really want you to own are cash conversion and return on invested capital. Cash conversion tells you whether the profit we report ever turns into cash in the bank. Plenty of companies report handsome profits and never see the money. Return on invested capital asks a blunter question — for every pound we've put in, how much are we getting back? If that number sits below what our funding costs, we are destroying value, however healthy the headline looks.

None of this is about making you sound like an accountant. It's so that when a paper says a division is 'strong', you can quietly ask which number says so.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why has James condensed the material onto a single page?
options: To save the company printing costs
Because the full diligence pack was confidential
So the director has only what she'll actually need, without decoding jargon alone
To test how quickly she can read financial documents
items.why: "I've put everything you'll actually need onto a single page… rather than leave you to decode the jargon alone."

items.q: What warning does James give about the word 'margin'?
options: It cannot be compared between companies
One must check which margin is meant, as gross and operating differ
It is rarely worth calculating
It always refers to gross margin
items.why: "be careful which margin someone means, because gross and operating are very different animals."

items.q: According to James, what does cash conversion reveal?
options: How fast the company is growing
How much debt the business carries
The dividend the board can safely pay
Whether reported profit actually turns into cash in the bank
items.why: "Cash conversion tells you whether the profit we report ever turns into cash in the bank."

items.q: What does James imply when he says a company can be 'destroying value, however healthy the headline looks'?
options: Value can only be measured over ten years
Healthy companies never destroy value
The headline figure is always falsified
Reported profit alone can hide poor returns on the capital invested
items.why: Inferência: se o retorno sobre o capital fica abaixo do custo do funding, o negócio destrói valor mesmo com lucro aparente — o número de manchete engana.

items.q: What is James's underlying intention in teaching her these terms?
options: To justify the size of the finance team
To make her sound like a professional accountant
To discourage her from questioning management
To give her the means to test a vague claim against a specific number
items.why: Inferência: "when a paper says a division is 'strong', you can quietly ask which number says so" — o objetivo é poder testar afirmações, não impressionar.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Below the industry benchmark, our return on invested capital barely covers the cost of the funding." This term measures…
options: the amount of cash held in reserve
the market value of the company's shares
the total revenue generated in a year
how much profit is earned for each unit of capital put into the business
items.why: Return on invested capital = retorno sobre o capital investido: quanto se ganha para cada unidade de capital empregada.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Strong reported profits mean little if ___ is weak and the money never reaches the bank."
options: reporting function
condescension
capital employed
cash conversion
items.why: Cash conversion = conversão de caixa: se é fraca, o lucro contábil não vira dinheiro em caixa.

items.q: "She explained each ratio without a trace of condescension." Condescension is…
options: a patronising, superior attitude toward others
excessive technical detail
impatience with slow learners
reluctance to share information
items.why: Condescension = condescendência: tratar alguém como inferior, com ar de superioridade.

items.q: "Every figure in the deck is testable against the ledger." Testable means that a figure…
options: is only an estimate
must be approved by the auditors
can be checked and verified against evidence
changes from quarter to quarter
items.why: Testable = testável: pode ser verificado contra os dados, em vez de apenas afirmado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The board could not properly ___ the proposal because it was described only in adjectives, not in numbers."
options: convert
evaluate
employ
report
items.why: To evaluate = avaliar: sem números, a diretoria não consegue avaliar a proposta.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de conselho e finanças. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The audit committee still has to sign off on the annual accounts." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve
publish externally
circulate for comment
postpone indefinitely
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the growth assumptions." They…
options: resisted or challenged them
postponed reading them
rewrote them entirely
approved them without question
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Once the board agrees the glossary, we'll roll it out to every committee." To roll out means to…
options: implement or introduce it in stages
test it in secret
summarise it briefly
quietly abandon it
items.why: Roll out = implementar/introduzir de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Better definitions won't move the needle unless the board actually uses them." This means they will…
options: take too long to measure
cost more than expected
make no noticeable difference
create internal resistance
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "She grasped the ratios quickly, but the real test is whether she follows through and questions vague claims." To follow through means to…
options: document the decision carefully
delegate the task to someone else
carry the intention all the way to action
revise the plan midway
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim, transformar a intenção em ação concreta.
